The built environment does not need more disconnected software. It needs better operating systems for how work gets done.That belief has shaped most of my career. Homebuilding and AEC are incredibly complex industries, but too much of the work still depends on fragmented tools, manual coordination, duplicated data, and processes that make good teams slower than they should be. I care about technology that changes that in practical, measurable ways.At Higharc, I help production homebuilders move toward a more connected operating model across design, estimating, sales, and construction. That work requires more than software implementation. It requires understanding how the business actually runs, aligning executives and department leaders, translating messy workflows into clear plans, and helping teams change without breaking the discipline that made them successful.My perspective comes from being close to the work itself: designing homes, building BIM standards, advising AEC and manufacturing firms, leading technology transformation programs, founding a residential design and consulting practice, helping build a software company, and serving in nonprofit leadership supporting Colorado’s AEC technology community.Those experiences have shaped how I lead. I try to be clear about the standard, direct with feedback, close to the work, and genuinely invested in the people doing it. The best teams I have been part of are serious about the craft, generous with each other, and motivated by work that matters.The work I find most meaningful is in building better teams, better tools, and better ways of working so we can design and deliver better homes, buildings, and communities.
